key_insight: 4DCodeBench evaluates whether AI agents can turn video into executable graphics code that recreates dynamic scenes, not just describe them. The benchmark tests if models can capture both scene structure and motion using compact programmatic representations.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of a benchmark for 4D inverse graphics: reconstructing dynamic, real-world scenes from video as code. This is a hard challenge because agents must infer objects, interactions, and physical behavior from visual observations alone.
method: Curate real-world videos and synthetic scenes with diverse dynamic behaviors to form benchmark tasks.
Ask agents to generate executable graphics programs that reconstruct the observed scenes over time.
Evaluate performance on how well the produced code captures scene structure, motion, and physical simulation.
impact: This benchmark gives AI/ML practitioners a concrete way to measure progress on video understanding, scene reconstruction, and code generation for dynamic environments. It can guide development of agents that reason about physics, causality, and temporal structure.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: video input -> scene inference -> executable graphics code -> reconstructed animation

Icons for motion, physics, code, and temporal sequence
paper_title: 4DCodeBench: Benchmarking Agents on Inverse Graphics of Dynamic Scenes
paper_authors: Ruihong Shen, Žiga Kovačič, Peter Kulits, Xingrui Wang, Zizhang Li
